steps.what: Sum stored quotes for property and equipment
Authorize the acquisition to increase efficiency

outputs: filed copy of signed capital authorization v1

tasks.design: A job sums stored quotes for equipment or property in {PROCUREMENT}. The manager recommends the capital expenditure and authorizes the acquisition. A later job files the signed authorization in {DOCS}. The sum is not the authorization, and the job does not buy the asset.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes were re-added before each capital request.
tasks.enabler_now: The quote lines are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A lower quote can still be the wrong asset.

ambition.what: Authorize or refuse a quote the week it is stored.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the authorization, not on adding quotes.

reach.task: Release funds only from the signed authorization

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a cost-to-serve figure is plain code on stored quantities and rates.

assumptions: Quote identifier, asset, and amount are stored on the procurement record. The procurement record produces them. A blank amount is not treated as zero. The job does not place the purchase.
Native configuration of the procurement record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining time is still the manager authorizing the acquisition.

incremental.description: Refresh quote identifier, asset, and amount when the procurement layout changes, and drop a total the manager has not accepted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes quote amounts are missing. The high end assumes quote identifier and amount are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored work orders and consumption reports
Issue work assignments for peak periods

outputs: filed copy of signed work assignments v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored work orders, consumption, invoices, and demand forecasts in {ERP}. The manager reviews them, estimates the peak, and issues the work assignments. A later job files the signed assignments in {DOCS}. The job does not assign a named person by a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders and forecasts were copied out before each assignment round.
tasks.still_hard: The peak is still a judgement, and the assignment is still the manager's.

ambition.what: Issue the week's assignments when the forecast is stored.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the peak and the assignments, not on collecting the rows.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says logistics planning is configured route and stock tools, and the manager decides.
Digest [S10] says no significant decision about a person is made solely by automation.
Digest [S11] says allocation or performance scoring of people is Annex III point 4(b).
Digest [S12] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Order identifier, consumption quantity, and forecast period are stored on the ledger. The ledger produces them. Assignments are written by the manager. No score of a person is produced.
Native configuration of the ledger is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining review time is still the manager reading the forecasts.

incremental.description: Refresh order identifier, consumption quantity, and forecast period when the ledger layout changes, and drop a list the manager has not reviewed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes forecast periods are missing. The high end assumes order identifier and forecast period are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The distribution manager spends the week on the floor, the exception, and the signed decision. A stored quantity times a stored rate, a rule on a document field, and filing that decision can move. The manager still directs people and still inspects the warehouse.
reach: A warehouse lead follows only the assignment the manager signed.
A carrier is told only the rate the manager signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a list that is missing a stored field.
Reject a procedure sentence that has no stored row.
role.ambitious_version: A signed operating decision can be filed the same week, and the manager still owns the floor.
